facts.statement: Priohybodus lived during the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous periods.
Priohybodus preyed primarily on fish and large vertebrates by grasping and cutting them.
facts.quote: preyed primarily on fish and large vertebrates grasping and cutting their prey

facts.statement: Priohybodus is grouped with Secarodus and Planohybodus in the informal group Priohybodontines.
facts.quote: It has been taxonomically grouped with Secarodus and Planohybodus into an informally named group Priohybodontines.

facts.statement: Priohybodus had a wide distribution across Gondwana, including Saharan Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, and South America.
facts.quote: Like many members of Hybodontiformes, this genus had a wide palaeogeographic distribution across Gondwana

facts.statement: Fossils of Priohybodus have been found in the Late Jurassic Mugher Mudstone in Ethiopia.
facts.quote: In Ethiopia, it is known from the Late Jurassic Mugher Mudstone.

facts.statement: Priohybodus was the first hybodontiform shark known to have fully serrated cutting edges on its teeth.
facts.quote: It has fully serrated cutting edges on its teeth and was the first hybodontiform shark known to develop this.

facts.statement: Priohybodus belongs to the family Hybodontidae.
Priohybodus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Priohybodus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Albian stages, between 154.8 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Albian (154.8 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Research suggests that the enameloid structure of Priohybodus arambourgi differs from that of modern sharks despite their similar external tooth morphology.
facts.quote: Evidence of differences in the structure of enameloid of Priohybodus arambourgi and modern sharks (in spite of similarities in external morphology of their teeth) is presented by Silva, Gallo & Eltink (2026).

rejected.statement: The genus was first described by Erasmo in 1960 based on fragmented and isolated tooth crowns found in a Late Jurassic formation in Somalia.
rejected.quote: The genus was first described by Erasmo in 1960 based on fragmented and isolated tooth crowns discovered in a Late Jurassic formation in Somalia.

rejected.statement: Priohybodus could grow up to 2 to 4 meters in length based on tooth size.
rejected.quote: It can grow up to 2 to 4 meters in length (based on tooth size)
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'to 4 meters in length based on tooth'
